newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ecopetrol lifts force majeure on oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol lifts force majeure on oil exports.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol lifted its declaration of force majeure at the Caribbean coast lifting terminal of Covenas shortly before 1600 local (2100 GMT) Monday, a spokesman said.
He said the revised program of loadings would be issued later in the day.

The spokesman said Ecopetrol had two cargoes totaling about 350,000 barrels waiting for immediate dispatch, one for Repsol, thought to be destined for the United States, and another for a refinery in Trinidad and Tobago.

Earlier in the day, a spokesman for Occidental Petroleum Corp, which operates the Cano Limon field in northeast Colombia, said a 1-million barrel consignment was waiting to be loaded for a U.S. Gulf Coast refinery.
Ecopetrol declared force majeure on oil exports from Covenas early a week ago after a series of leftist rebel attacks on the pipeline that pumps crude from the Cano Limon field.
